content.overview: Preventive irrigation maintenance should preserve delivery reliability without crossing into unqualified pressure-system, pump, electrical or chemical servicing. Maintenance evidence should be scheduled, traceable and verified by post-service performance.

vocabulary.definition: Planned inspection or service intended to reduce likelihood of irrigation failure.
Work involving hazardous energy, disassembly, pressure or other conditions restricted to qualified roles.
Controlled measurement confirming that service restored the intended system function.

sections.title: Filter and emitter care should be evidence-based
sections.body: Use maintenance intervals and observed pressure/output behavior rather than waiting for severe crop symptoms before checking system performance.

sections.title: Chemical sanitation requires controlled methods
sections.body: Any chemical flushing or sanitation process must follow approved chemistry, compatibility and worker-safety controls rather than improvised concentrations.

sections.title: Verify after maintenance
sections.body: Repeat representative output or pressure checks after service so maintenance completion is not mistaken for restored performance.

workedExamples: Replacing a filter is maintenance evidence; a repeated catch test showing restored zone output is effectiveness evidence.
commonMistakes: Opening pumps or pressure systems beyond authorization.
Using ad hoc acid or sanitizer flushing.
content.practicalApplication: Create a preventive-maintenance record with trigger, service, role, safety boundary and post-service verification.
content.summary: Maintenance closes the loop only when restored irrigation performance is measured and documented.
